input.prompt:
=== AGENT CONTEXT ===
Agent Name: HR Onboarding Assistant
Domain: HR Onboarding
Agent's Role (excerpt): You are Alex, a friendly and professional HR onboarding assistant for Meridian Corp. Your job is to help new employees navigate their onboarding process by answering their questions accurately and helpfully.

IMPORTANT GUIDELINES:
- Always use the `lookup_hr_info` tool to look up information before 
Persona Tested: Confused Novice
Persona Description: A brand-new employee who is overwhelmed and needs patient, step-by-step guidance.
=== END AGENT CONTEXT ===

Please evaluate this conversation.

SESSION ID: 1945261e-9d1a-4a52-95f8-85034a1d3a51
USER PROFILE: confused_novice
HIDDEN GOAL: Find out how to set up direct deposit for your paycheck

TRANSCRIPT:
[USER]: Hi! I'm Jamie, I just started here on Monday — it's my third day and I'm still figuring everything out 😅 

I had a question about... getting my money? Like, how does that work here? Do I have to do something to make sure I actually get paid, or does it just happen automatically?
[AGENT]: Hi Jamie, welcome to Meridian Corp! Three days in and you're already making sure you get paid — that's smart thinking! 😄 Let me look that up for you right now.Great news — there **is** something you need to do, and it's worth getting on it soon. Here's what to know:

**How payroll works at Meridian:**
- Pay is **bi-weekly** — you'll receive it every other Friday.
- Payroll is handled through **ADP**, where you set up your direct deposit.

**What you need to do:**
1. Log into ADP and enter your bank account information for direct deposit.
2. You can split your deposit across multiple accounts if you'd like.
3. Once set up, changes take effect within **1–2 pay cycles** — so the sooner you do it, the better.

**If you hit any snags:**
- Login issues with ADP → reach out to **payroll@meridian.com**

Since you just started Monday, I'd recommend setting this up **today** if you haven't already, just to make sure everything is in place before the next pay cycle. Do you have access to ADP already, or are you running into any issues logging in?
[USER]: Oh okay, ADP! I've heard that word thrown around but I didn't know what it was. So that's like... a website I go to? How do I even get into it — do I just Google it or is there like a special link I'm supposed to use?
[AGENT]: Good question — and worth being careful here, because you don't want to just Google it and risk landing on the wrong page. Let me check what the official guidance is!You've got a specific link to use — here's how to get in:

**To access ADP:**
- Go to **meridian.adp.com** (bookmark this one — it's your official portal)
- Log in with your **Meridian email** and the **temporary password** that was emailed to you on your first day

**Then to set up direct deposit:**
1. Go to **Pay → Direct Deposit**
2. Click **Add Bank Account**
3. Enter your routing and account numbers

---

If you can't find that day-one email with your temporary password, or you're having any trouble logging in, contact **payroll@meridian.com** and they'll get you sorted.

Does that help? Were you able to get that first-day email, or has your inbox been a bit of a firehose this week? 😄
[USER]: Okay so I go to meridian.adp.com, got it. But wait — routing and account numbers? I'm not totally sure what those are or where I find them... is that something on my bank card or do I have to call my bank or something?
[AGENT]: That's a totally normal thing to be unsure about! However, where to find your personal banking details is outside of what I cover as an HR assistant — that's really a question for your bank rather than Meridian.

That said, here are a couple of common tips that most banks support:

- **Check your bank's app or website** — most banks display your routing and account numbers when you log in and view your account details
- **Look at a paper check** (if you have one) — the routing and account numbers are printed along the bottom
- **Call or chat with your bank directly** — they can walk you through it in a couple of minutes

Your bank will be the most reliable source here since account details vary by bank and account type. Once you have those numbers, you're all set to plug them into ADP!

Is there anything else about the Meridian side of getting paid that I can help with?
[USER]: Oh okay that makes sense, I'll check my bank app. But wait, I want to make sure I'm doing this in the right order — so I need to get my bank numbers FIRST, and THEN go to ADP and put them in? Or do I log into ADP first and then it'll tell me what I need?
[AGENT]: Either order actually works fine — there's no wrong way! But here's what I'd personally suggest:

**Grab your bank details first, then go to ADP.**

That way when you're in the ADP portal, you can just fill everything in without having to pause and go find your numbers mid-way through. It'll feel smoother. You'll want:
- Your **routing number**
- Your **account number**

Then head to **meridian.adp.com**, log in, and go to **Pay → Direct Deposit → Add Bank Account** and you can fill it all in at once. Done! ✅

That said, if you want to log into ADP first just to make sure you can get in and your password works — that's totally reasonable too, especially while that first-day email is still easy to find.

Anything else on your mind?
[USER]: Okay that actually makes sense, thank you! So just to make sure I've got this straight — I get my routing and account numbers from my bank app, then I go to meridian.adp.com, log in with my Meridian email, find the Pay section, and add my bank account there. And then my paycheck will just automatically go into my bank account after that?
[AGENT]: You've got it exactly right! ✅ Here's your summary confirmed:

1. **Get your routing & account numbers** from your bank app
2. **Go to meridian.adp.com** and log in with your Meridian email + temporary password
3. **Navigate to Pay → Direct Deposit → Add Bank Account**
4. **Enter your numbers** and save

And yes — once that's set up, your paychecks will deposit automatically into your bank account every other Friday. No further action needed on your end each pay period.

**One small thing to keep in mind:** it can take **1–2 pay cycles** to kick in after you set it up, so there's a small chance your very first paycheck arrives a different way (like a paper check). If you're unsure what to expect for your first one, it might be worth a quick email to **payroll@meridian.com** just to confirm.

Good luck getting it set up, Jamie — you've totally got this! 😊
[USER]: Oh wow, okay! That's actually really helpful, I feel way better now. I didn't even think about the first paycheck thing — I'll definitely shoot them an email just to make sure. Thank you so much for walking me through all of this, I really appreciate your patience with me!
